question: Is the task1 deficit in the mixed-batch8 run characterized by max-horizon truncation in the five paired initializations that succeeded under the same-seed homogeneous joint4 reference?
falsifiable_hypothesis: At least 4 of the 5 old-only task1 paired successes (old homogeneous joint4 succeeds, new mixed-batch8 fails) terminate the new run at max_steps=300, while their old successful counterparts finish before step 260. Fewer than four such pairs, or old successful counterparts at/after 260, falsifies this registered horizon-phenotype hypothesis.

comparison.old: seed2001 homogeneous joint4 batch2, 160k, registered paired task1 init0..19
comparison.matched_initialization_provenance: Previously verified exact match for 20/20 task1 paired starts across model-array inputs, simulator state, frame/input/images, processor, and RNG; model weights intentionally differ.

method: Read only per-episode success, steps, max_steps from the two existing completion.json summaries for task1 paired init0..19. Report the registered horizon phenotype counts and complete per-pair step pairs; do not inspect or alter raw trajectories, videos, action arrays, checkpoints, or training logs.
interpretation_limits: Post-hoc diagnostic on one seed; not a causal estimate.
The contrast changes batch size and gradient co-averaging together.
Horizon truncation phenotype does not prove undertraining or multi-task interference.
A negative result does not pass or change any registered gate.
